slides.title: 7 Little Laws Smart People _Quietly_ Follow
slides.sub: Save these. You'll use them every week.

slides.title: 1. Kidlin's Law
slides.sub: A worry in your head is fog. Write the problem down clearly and it's half solved.

slides.title: 2. Pareto's Law

graphic.q: Which 2 of your 10 tasks are the gold ones?

slides.sub: Roughly 80% of your results come from 20% of your effort. (A rule of thumb, not an exact law.)

slides.title: 3. Murphy's Law

graphic.note: Plan for it once. Then stop worrying about it.

slides.sub: Anything that can go wrong, will. That's not a reason to panic. It's a reason to prepare.

slides.title: 4. Wilson's Law

graphic.q: Keep building. The money tends to catch up.

slides.sub: Put knowledge first, and money tends to follow, but usually later than the effort.

slides.title: 5. Gilbert's Law

graphic.prompt: Boss: “Can you sort out the client report?”

options.t: Propose the best way, then do it

graphic.q: Which one gets trusted with more?

slides.sub: Nobody will tell you exactly what to do. Working out the best way is part of the job.

slides.title: 6. Falkland's Law
slides.sub: When you don't have to make a decision, don't. Rushing adds pressure and mistakes.

slides.title: 7. Hick's Law

graphic.q: How many tabs do you have open right now?

slides.sub: The more options you have, the longer it takes to choose, and the less sure you feel.

slides.title: Which One Do You Break Most?

graphic.q: Which of the 7 laws do you break most often?

slides.sub: Pick one law and use it this week. Small rules make a big difference.
